user.title: EKM Push3 gateway
user.description: Enter the gateway's address and its local API key (the `key` parameter of a readMeter URL).

data_description.host: The integration polls the gateway's readMeter API over HTTP.

data.name: Name
data.legacy_prefix: Existing entity ID prefix to take over (optional)

data_description.name: Device name; entity names are added to it.
data_description.legacy_prefix: If this meter is already set up with REST sensors, enter their common prefix (for example sensor.house_power). The next step matches existing entities by suffix (_total_watts, _total_energy, _l1_amps, ...) so they keep their entity IDs, history and Energy dashboard references.

adopt.title: Take over entities for {name}
adopt.description:
Each entity ID listed here moves to meter {address} and keeps its history, statistics, settings and Energy dashboard references. Clear a field to create a new entity instead.

Setup waits and retries until the REST sensors (or other sources) providing these IDs are removed.

data_description.api_key: Leave empty to keep the current key.

error.invalid_key: The gateway rejected the request. Check the API key.
error.invalid_response: The host did not return EKM meter readings.
error.invalid_entity_id: Enter a sensor entity ID, such as sensor.house_power_total_watts.
error.duplicate_entity_id: The same entity ID is used twice.
error.wrong_gateway: That gateway doesn't serve any of this entry's meters.

data_description.stale_after: A meter whose latest reading at the gateway is older than this counts as not communicating (for example, it lost power) and its entities go unavailable. Keep it at least a few polling intervals long.
data_description.correct_meter: Use when this meter's CTs also see another meter's load (for example, a downstream feeder passing through a main CT). Its total power and energy have the other meter's subtracted. Choose None to stop; energy stays continuous either way.
data_description.correct_by: The meter whose load is being double-counted.
data_description.scale_meter: Use when a CT on this meter reads high or low by a known factor (for example, the wrong CT ratio). Each line's current and power are multiplied by its scale, and total power and energy are rebuilt from the corrected lines. Choose None, or leave every scale at 1, to stop; energy stays continuous either way.
data_description.scale_l1: Multiplier for line 1. A CT reading 1.8 times too high needs 0.556 (1 divided by 1.8).
data_description.scale_auto: Apply each line's scale only while its CT is misreading: the line's current is compared with the other lines' average, over the averaging window. Off: the scale always applies.
data_description.scale_on: The scale is applied once the averaged ratio reaches this (for example 1.15 when the line normally runs at 0.7–1.0 of the others).
data_description.scale_off: The scale is released once the averaged ratio falls to this. Keep it below the apply ratio.
data_description.scale_delay: How long the ratio is averaged before switching.

error.correct_by_invalid: Choose a different meter to subtract.
error.meter_not_reading: That meter has no reading yet; try again in a moment.
error.scale_thresholds_invalid: The release ratio must be below the apply ratio.
